podcast.title: Joined The Coasters (1957)
podcast.body: Cornel Gunter joined The Coasters, replacing Leon Hughes, as part of the classic lineup that formed in 1957. "When we last left the coasters, they'd just taken on two new singers. Cornel Gunter and Doug Jones, to replace Leon Hughes and Bobby Nun."

srcs.source: A History of Rock Music in 500 Songs

podcast.title: Murder (1990)
podcast.body: Cornel Gunter was shot dead in 1990, and his killer has never been found. "And finally Gunter himself was shot dead in 1990 and his killer has never been found."

srcs.source: A History of Rock Music in 500 Songs

podcast.title: Departure from The Coasters
podcast.body: Shortly after the release of "Little Egypt," The Coasters' last significant hit, Cornel Gunter decided to leave the group. He took up an opportunity to sing in Dinah Washington's backing group. "Shortly after its release Cornel Gunter decided to leave the group and take up an opportunity to sing in Diana Washington's backing group."

srcs.source: A History of Rock Music in 500 Songs

podcast.title: Fired by Dinah Washington
podcast.body: After joining Dinah Washington's backing group, Cornel Gunter was soon sacked by her. This led him to form his own group. "Unfortunately Gunter was soon sacked by Diana Washington and he decided to form his own group and to call it The Coasters."

srcs.source: A History of Rock Music in 500 Songs

podcast.title: Formed Rival "The Coasters" Group
podcast.body: After being sacked by Dinah Washington, Cornel Gunter formed his own group, which he also called "The Coasters." The other three members of his new group had previously been members of The Penguins, a vocal group Gunter had known for years and came out of the same musical "stew" as. "Unfortunately Gunter was soon sacked by Diana Washington and he decided to form his own group and to call it The Coasters."

srcs.source: A History of Rock Music in 500 Songs

podcast.title: Recording and Touring with His Group
podcast.body: Cornel Gunter's version of The Coasters was not permitted to record under "The Coasters" name, so they made records credited as "Cornel Gunter and The Coasters." However, his group was able to tour under "The Coasters" name and was a cheaper option than the original studio group. Dick Clark, a friend of Gunter, began booking Gunter's version of the group for tours. "Gunter's group weren't allowed to record as The Coasters so they made records just under Gunter's own name whereas Cornel Gunter and The Coasters."

srcs.source: A History of Rock Music in 500 Songs

podcast.title: Shining on "One by One" Album
podcast.body: Despite usually being relegated to backing roles due to his sweeter voice not suiting the group's usual lead material, Cornel Gunter impressed critics on The Coasters' "One by One" album. He took solo lead on three songs, showcasing his admiration for singer Dinah Washington through his imitations of her style. "To the extent that anyone noticed it at all, they mostly commented on how good Cornell Gunter sounded."

srcs.source: A History of Rock Music in 500 Songs

podcast.title: Sister's Answer Record to "Yakati Yak"
podcast.body: Cornel Gunter's sister, Glorvia Gunter, released an answer record to The Coasters' hit "Yakati Yak," on which Cornel himself sang backing vocals. "The song was successful enough that it spawned a few answer records, including one by Cornel Gunter's sister Glorvia, which Cornel sang backing vocals on."

srcs.source: A History of Rock Music in 500 Songs

podcast.title: Vocal Arranger for The Coasters
podcast.body: Within the new Coasters lineup, Cornel Gunter took on the role of working out the group's vocal arrangements. "Cornel Gunter would work out the group's vocal arrangements."

srcs.source: A History of Rock Music in 500 Songs
